title: TaskRequest
description: What starts a task: an OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693), shown as JSON; on the wire it is form-encoded, with authorization_details as a JSON string (RFC 9396). For a user task an application sends it with the user's ID token and gets a one-time ticket for the agent. For a service task the agent's sidecar sends it with the agent's own token and gets the grant.

subject_token.description: Who the task is for. A user task: an ID token from one of the application's idps, or a JWT the application signed when its users are self_asserted. A service task: the agent's own identity token.

requested_token_type.description: A user task asks for a ticket; a service task asks for the grant itself.

authorization_details.description: Exactly one agent_task entry: which task, about which object, for which agent, started how.

confirmation.description: Proof that the user confirmed this exact task: a JWT signed by the application (private_key_jwt) or by the identity provider, with claims sub (the user), task_type, object_id, agent and iat. Required when the task type's start.confirmation is user.

client_assertion.description: The application's signed JWT, for private_key_jwt (RFC 7523 §2.2). Other callers send neither field.

agentTask.description: The task to start. The scope comes from the task type, never from the request.

object_id.description: ID of the object the task is about; it must match the task type's id_pattern.

agent.description: The agent that will run the task.

trigger.description: How the task came about; it must be one of the task type's triggers.
